author: Fluid_Pie_9428
body:
Panda is definitely a must have, second reliable AOE summon

Mammoth can be decent at PvP and as a tank (half of the hp of AD and same if not bigger damage)

Penguin is good for raids 

Turtle is a nice defensive buffer + Stone stare 

Coral is a good summon overall (for the time it's available at least)

Beaver has the capability of VSS (wallop) and some self sustainable ward skills

Gorilla is complete ass, unless you're collecting every summon in the game, don't buy it

Plus all of them have collateral damage so everyone has potential for aoe (since if the enemy they attack dies from their initial attack, CD damage goes to a random enemy)

author: isol8id
body:
As a lvl 241 GSA who doesn't really know anything:

* Penguin - on average deals more damage than Ancient Dragon but has much lower HP so battles require more micromanagement. They cast Deific Channel on themselves fairly regularly and go from doing (at my level) about 25k damage per hit to over 100k - something that would take *a lot* of buffing for AD to achieve. Totally useless for endless and towers as there probably won't be time for them to cast DC.

Edit: Pengu's attack, Beastrikes, uses crit hits - this might be buffable to hit higher numbers too.

* Panda - Keep hearing that it's a better Ancient Jinn, it's definitely tankier with more HP and it's elementless AOE attack means it's less likely to be resisted/immuned against by an enemy but I've found it deals less damage but it all depends on what it's up against.

* Mammoth - in testing I've found it dealt less damage than Penguins and Ancient Dragon and haven't felt the need to use it. If it castes Divine Bastion on itself it might become tankier but with AD and Great Hydra available at T10 this isn't an issue. It's mixed-element attack could come in handy if you know what you'll be up against, but AD can cast Dragon Blight which makes the target weak against it's Dragon attacks anyway.

* Timber - haven't bought :/

Anyway that's my 2 cents but honestly I'm not into min/maxing and looking at the deeper stats. Generally I like to set up a team, buff them and then switch my brain off and these new summons require more forward thinking and management than I can be bothered with!

I'd love to be proved wrong though and I'm open to any new synergies or strategies for these new summons.
